messages.content: What is TernOO-5500FP?

TernOO-5500FP is a 24-trit balanced-ternary computer architecture. Its CPU (the 5500FP) has 81 registers and a word format of 2+4+18 trits: T23-T22 the primary field, T22-T19 the qualifier, and T18-T0 the payload. It is balanced ternary — each trit is -1, 0, or +1 — so the cleverness lives in the architecture, not in silicon wizardry.
What are the nine primary word types in TernOO?

The nine primaries are equal peers with no hierarchy between them: DATA, EXEC, MAP, NEURAL, I-O, CRYPTO (reserved), OPEN_B, POOL, and OPCODE. Structure is packed into the three fields; every word is self-describing without asking anything else.
What is FlowCode?

FlowCode is TernOO's visual programming environment: the diagram IS the program. A flowchart of symbols and edges compiles to a stream of TernOO words, which the emulator runs and PIGART renders on screen — the same word stream, seen from different points of view. FlowCode is language-agnostic; it wrote machine words because that was the only TernOO-native thing there was.
What makes a FlowCode program a FlowCode program?

The flowchart. At minimum a FlowCode program is a flowchart of flow symbols (terminators, processes, decisions, loops, I/O) joined by edges. A GUI design is added only if the program has a GUI, and a sheet only if there is maths. The flowchart is what distinguishes it from raw TernOO words.
How is a GUI widget represented in the TernOO word stream?

A widget is a PIGART RNODE instruction span under the OPCODE family: an RNODE opcode word plus MAP (position), DATA (dimensions), DATA/SCALAR (kind), and USER-DEF (bound object). Its properties ride as MPROP words, signal bindings as MBIND words (targets by name), and a control's value as an MVALUE DATA word in its span. No new primary family is needed.
How is containment expressed between widgets?

By edges in the stream, not by packed offsets. A child's parent is named via an MSCOPE word; position and membership belong to the container (stream order, the containing span, an edge word), never packed into the leaf.
State the intrinsic-versus-relational law.

A word carries its intrinsic properties and never its relational ones. Intrinsic = what it is on its own with no other word in the world (glyph identity, case, font, colour). Relational = position, membership, neighbours, size-in-context — these belong to the container. Build order is free; inheritance direction is not: the child must never know the string.
How is a text character stored in TernOO's native glyph plane?

A character is one DATA/STRING word in the native plane (T19 = +1). Its payload after the 23-09 ruling: X tribble (T17-T12) = identity (T17 case trit, T16-T12 signed ordinal, 0 = null); Y tribble (T11-T6) = font pointer (0 = inherit); Z tribble (T5-T0) = colour cube (0 = inherit ink). Reads identity to font to colour.
Why was 'King X' deposed in the glyph plane?

The X field used to hold a character's position within its string. That is a relational property packed into a leaf — the container already expresses order — so it violated the intrinsic-versus-relational law and nothing ever read it. Position was vacated to the container; the freed tribble now carries colour.
How does TernOO encode colour?

As a balanced-ternary cube in six trits: two trits per channel for R, G, B, nine levels each, giving 729 = 3^6 colours. All-zero means inherit the default ink. A 27-colour traffic-light/LED palette is the higher trit of each pair — an exact subset of the fine cube, so an LED red is the same word as a text red.
What are the tri-state controls in the TernUI widget kit?

Controls that are balanced-ternary by birthright: gui_tritoggle (-/0/+), gui_trifilter (include/exclude/don't-care), and gui_tritstrip. Their value lives as a DATA word in the widget's span so the stream stays self-describing and the value can travel as a word-diff delta.
What is DICK in the TernOO project?

DICK is the Deterministic Inference Colony Kernel: an all-integer inference/training kernel whose runs are bit-identical across machines and replayable. Its doctrine is to optimise the deployment criterion directly and validate token-exact against a reference — determinism as a sellable audit primitive.
What is the R1 rule on the CompuCoin ledger?

R1: credit minted from training work pays a balance but is never burnable. It is enforced structurally by an allow-list — only weight-bearing vote classes may burn — so the next work class arrives non-burnable by construction.
What is the TernOO north star for the next object model?

A second, vertical object model (Desktop, Window, Canvas, String, Char) is emerging on top of the flat word model. It must be MADE OF flat words — a class is a span-of-spans, inheritance is an edge word — never a second truth beside them. A language called TOOL will carry it, and TOOL always compiles down to words or it is scaffolding.
How should TOOL's design be approached?

Three-way split: semantics EMERGE (extracted from the widget campaign specimens, not designed ahead); the surface syntax is DESIGNED for humans (a disposable face over the semantics); and substrate is not scaffold — C that stands in for the machine (emulator, framebuffer) is fine, C that stands in for TernOO code is the forbidden line. Everything above the framebuffer is words.
What is PIGART?

PIGART is TernOO's native rendering layer: it draws the program from the same word stream the emulator runs. A FlowCode diagram on the canvas is PIGART rendering RNODE/REDGE words — the diagram that runs.
What is P2PCP?

P2PCP is TernOO's peer-to-peer compute mesh: nodes trade real local model inference and native 5500FP compute for CompuCoin over a LAN or tailnet. It has discovery, resilience, reputation, persistence, and a governance loop of earn, burn, vote, slash.
Who is the Professor in the TernOO project?

The Professor is the ship's local language-model persona, served on the compute mesh. Its role is a tutor for GHOST and an offline assistant — an encyclopedia and thinking partner when the internet is down. Its brain is OLMo-2-7B, chosen because it is genuinely trainable, so it can be taught ship fluency rather than only prompted.
Why is TernOO well suited to lean or old hardware?

Because its efficiency is architectural, not borrowed from a modern CPU's speculative silicon. A lean, predictable word-stream interpreter degrades gracefully on simple hardware where bloated VMs collapse, and it is an ideal fit for clean RISC chips and, eventually, native ternary silicon where the binary-emulation tax vanishes.
What does the FlowCode canvas represent to the user?

From the user's point of view the canvas IS the program — the visual diagram they see and edit. From the processor's point of view the program is the TernOO words in memory. Both are the same artifact seen from different perspectives; PIGART renders the words as the diagram.
